newsitem.title: USA: Midwest Cash Grain PM -Selling interest light.
newsitem.headline: Midwest Cash Grain PM -Selling interest light.

text.p: A lower close in CBOT futures on Thursday shut off farmer interest in selling soybeans or corn, U.S. Midwest merchandisers said.
"We're certainly not buying anything now," said a dealer in central Indiana.
CBOT soybeans settled two to 11-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with August down two cents at $7.46 per bushel and September corn was down 2-3/4 at $2.34-1/2.
August soybeans recovered from a 19-cent drop to end two cents per bushel lower. That recovery put some flat prices back near $8.00 per bushel, and some sales were reported.
Soybean river basis values were lower in response to a drop in prices at the U.S. Gulf, dealers said.

Cool temperatures in the northeastern Corn Belt were said to be delaying the start of the soft red winter wheat harvest. Trade sources had initially expected harvest in that area to begin by the end of this week.
"We're trying to get the wheat started, but these cool temperatures are not helping," a Toledo dealer said. "We need warmer temperatures for that last little burst of growth."
Basis values are quoted against CBOT futures, cash $/bu.

Note: UNQ=Unquoted. N=CBOT July, Q=CBOT August, U=CBOT Sept
